# Oxford English Dictionary

> > The Oxford English Dictionary (OED) is the definitive historical dictionary of the English language, documenting word meanings, etymologies, pronunciations, and usage from Old English to the present day.

The OED provides comprehensive lexicographic entries for over 600,000 words, tracing their evolution through citations from historical texts, literary works, and scientific publications. Each entry includes detailed etymology, pronunciation guides, usage examples, and frequency data across different time periods and varieties of English.

## Key Topics

- etymology
- historical linguistics
- lexicography
- word history
- pronunciation guide
- Latin borrowings
- obsolete words
- historical usage
- French loanwords
- Greek origins
- word frequency
- Old English
- Middle English
- linguistic variation
- semantic change

- [Abbasid, n. & adj.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbasid_n): Dictionary entry for 'Abbasid' with Latin etymology and historical usage
- [Aaron's serpent, n.](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/aarons-serpent_n): Dictionary entry for biblical term 'Aaron's serpent' with Pope citation
